Nothing about the desktop tile look changed (he prefers the current wider tiles at 1920x1080); the only desktop changes are the apostrophe and the search position, and everything else was added purely as a smaller-screen fallback. 1. Apostrophe: the hero subtitle showed "you'''re" (three apostrophes) from a baked-in shell-escape artifact in coverage.ts; now "you're". 2. Search containment (Luneth chose "contain to content, same row"): the search bar was floating mid-right and spilling past the content column toward the telemetry. Fix: give the topbar the same 380px right reserve as the coverage content/panel split, and right-align the command box, so its right edge now lands exactly on the hero box's right edge (measured cmd.right == hero.right == 1468 at 1920). Also nowrap+ellipsis on the placeholder so it never wraps into a tall box on narrow screens. 3. Responsive fallback (his "main win" -- works on all devices) with the hard constraint that 1920 stays byte-identical. The core fix was a classic CSS grid blowout: the shell's 220px/1fr column grew past the viewport because 1fr floors at min-content. Switching app-shell + coverage-grid + coverage-hero__head to minmax(0,1fr) and adding min-width:0 to coverage-main lets the content shrink -- and since minmax(0,1fr)==1fr when content fits, 1920 is unchanged. Then additive max-width breakpoints: at 1160 the DAILY PROTOCOL panel stacks below the periodic table (topbar panel-reserve released, redundant subtitle hidden); at 820 the left rail collapses to a 60px icon bar; at 560 (phone) the hero stat stacks under the title, tiles shrink to fit, breadcrumb/footer trim.
